atomic_facts.fact: Rodrigo Rato served as Managing Director (chief) of the International Monetary Fund.
Rato is a former (not current) IMF chief; his IMF tenure has ended.
Rodrigo Rato served as Managing Director of the IMF.
His IMF tenure ran from 2004 to 2007.
On 20 December 2024, a Madrid court sentenced Rodrigo Rato.
The prison sentence was more than four years.
He was convicted of tax crimes, money laundering and corruption.
The convictions included three offences against the Treasury (delitos contra la Hacienda Pública).
Rodrigo Rato was convicted by a Madrid court in December 2024.
The conviction was for tax fraud, money laundering and corruption.
The conviction was the culmination of judicial proceedings, with judges finding Rato guilty after a trial.
Judges found Rato guilty of three offences against the Treasury.
Rato was not acquitted of the offences against the Treasury.
The charges for the Treasury offences were not dropped; they proceeded to a guilty verdict.
The only acquittal mentioned (Bankia 2012 listing) was in a separate trial, distinct from the Treasury offences.
The Audiencia Nacional agreed that Rodrigo Rato, among other former PP ministers/leaders, should appear in the Gürtel trial.
The appearance was to be as a witness (testigo).
